item.research_question: How do the micromechanical properties, specifically elastic stability, anisotropy, ideal shear strength, and dislocation core width, compare between fcc and hcp phases of polymorphic high-entropy alloys?
item.material_system: Five 3d transition metal HEAs: Cr25Fe25Co25Ni25, Cr20Mn20Fe20Co20Ni20, Cr20Mn20Fe30Co20Ni10, Cr20Mn20Fe34Co20Ni6, and Cr10Mn30Fe50Co10
item.processing_route: First-principles simulations using density-functional theory (DFT) with the exact muffin-tin orbitals method (EMTO) and coherent-potential approximation (CPA); calculations performed in paramagnetic state with Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof functional
item.test_conditions: Zero temperature and pressure; shear loading on (111) planes for fcc and (0001) basal planes for hcp; two modes considered: no relaxation and relaxation allowed after each shear step
key_findings: All five HEAs are elastically stable in both fcc and hcp phases at zero temperature and pressure.

In the hcp phase, polycrystalline moduli decrease with increasing valence electron concentration (VEC), with variations of ~38% for shear modulus G, ~36% for Young's modulus E, and ~26% for bulk modulus B.
In the fcc phase, Young's modulus E and shear modulus G reduce until VEC reaches ≈ 8, then slightly increase.
For VEC ≤ 8, hcp phases exhibit larger Young's modulus E, bulk modulus B, and shear modulus G than their fcc counterparts.
The ideal shear strength (ISS) of hcp Cr20Mn20Fe20Co20Ni20 is 11.7 GPa, which is more than two times larger than its fcc phase value of 4.4 GPa.
Relaxation during shearing reduces the ISS by 22% for Cr20Mn20Fe30Co20Ni10 and 20% for Cr20Mn20Fe20Co20Ni20 in the hcp phase.

The half-width of the dislocation core (ζ) for fcc Cr20Mn20Fe20Co20Ni20 is 3.89 Å, which is more than two times larger than the ζ values of 1.57 Å and 1.53 Å for the hcp phases of Cr20Mn20Fe30Co20Ni10 and Cr20Mn20Fe20Co20Ni20, respectively.
The fcc structure is elastically more anisotropic than the hcp structure across the studied alloys.
item.mechanism: The higher ISS in hcp is attributed to its ABAB stacking sequence acting as an intermediate case between the 'soft' and 'hard' shear directions of fcc, leading to a more rapid energy increase. The larger dislocation core width in fcc reduces the Peierls barrier, explaining its increased ductility compared to hcp.
item.limitations: The study did not investigate possible phonon instabilities during the relaxation of the computational cell.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the findings provide atomic-level knowledge for the intelligent design of further high-entropy materials.
quotes: The hcp phase possesses more than two times larger intrinsic strength than that of the fcc phase.
The derived half-width of the dislocation core predicts a smaller Peierls barrier in the fcc phase confirming its increased ductility compared to the hcp one.
We find that the decreases are about 20% and 16% for G and E, respectively.
